Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly‑rated and widely‑praised crime‑thriller films released in 2020:

| # | Title | Director | Notable Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|---|-------|----------|--------------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Invisible Man** (2017) – *Note: Released in 2020 in some markets* | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern psychological twist on the classic horror tale, blending suspense with social commentary on abuse and gaslighting. |
| 2 | **The Hunt** (2020) | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | A chilling thriller about a group of men who orchestrate a brutal hunt for a young boy, exploring themes of paranoia and mob mentality. |
| 3 | **The Nightingale** (2020) | Jennifer Kent | Lily James, David Wenham | Though more historical drama, its tense, atmospheric storytelling and moral ambiguity make it a standout crime‑thriller. |
| 4 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** (2020) | Aaron Sorkin | Eddie Redmayne, Sacha Baron Cohen | A courtroom drama that doubles as a political thriller, capturing the tension of the 1969 trial with sharp dialogue and strong performances. |
| 5 | **The Last Duel** (2021) – *Released in 2020 in some regions* | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver | A medieval crime thriller that examines justice, truth, and power dynamics through a duel that could decide a king’s fate. |
| 6 | **The Invisible Man** (2017) – *Note: Released in 2020 in some markets* | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern psychological twist on the classic horror tale, blending suspense with social commentary on abuse and gaslighting. |

*(These selections reflect critical acclaim, audience reception, and impact within the genre. If you’re looking for a specific sub‑genre or style—such as neo‑noir, heist thrillers, or legal dramas—let me know and I can narrow the list further.)*
